title: AISC benchmark Case 2 (P-Delta and P-delta), US table, with shear deformation, P = 100

source.work: ANSI/AISC 360-22, Specification for Structural Steel Buildings (American Institute of Steel Construction), Commentary
source.notes: input data and targets read on the cited page; nothing of the source is reproduced. Section properties of the W14x48 are not given by the source and are not taken from any table: I_x is calibrated on the source's own P = 0 deflection without shear deformation of Case 2, the shear flexibility on the source's P = 0 deflections with and without shear deformation (see build_problems.py and README.md)
source.location: Commentary Section C2.1, Fig. C-C2.3 (benchmark problem Case 2), US customary table, column P = 100, unbracketed values

analysis: Case 2 of the source: fixed-base cantilever under a lateral load of 1.0 kip and the axial compression P at the top; targets: moment at the base and lateral deflection of the top. Axial load level P = 100 x 1 kip (load case P holds the unit axial load, the combination factor is the level). US customary table: E = 29,000 ksi, L = 28.0 ft = 336 in, I = 483.92 in^4 (calibrated, see source.notes), G A_s = 56000 kip (calibrated on the P = 0 column of this case; shear deformation included: the source's unbracketed values). Member vertical along global Z, bending in the X-Z plane about local z (the section's Iz = Iy = I). Second-order analysis; the engine's member carries the exact stability functions, so one member is the exact solution of the second-order theory. The support idealisation is read from the source's sketch.

targets.precisionNote: stated tolerance 0.03 on printed "470"; acceptance criterion stated by the source on the same page (AISC 360-22 Commentary C2.1, p. 16.1-337): moments within 3 %, deflections within 5 %; value printed to 3 significant figures
targets.sign: magnitude in the source; in the engine's convention (member local x upward, local y = global +X, loads along +X) the midspan moment Mz of Case 1 is negative and the base moment of Case 2 positive

targets.precisionNote: stated tolerance 0.05 on printed "1.34"; acceptance criterion stated by the source on the same page (AISC 360-22 Commentary C2.1, p. 16.1-337): moments within 3 %, deflections within 5 %; value printed to 3 significant figures
targets.sign: magnitude in the source; the load acts along +X, deflection +X

limitsNote: Section properties are calibrated on the source's own P = 0 values (the source gives none): the problem verifies the second-order amplification, not section properties. It does NOT test shear deformation: the source's acceptance tolerance (3 % on moments, 5 % on deflections) is wider than the whole effect of shear deformation in its tables (at most 1.3 % on a moment and 3.5 % on a deflection between the bracketed and unbracketed values), so these targets would also be met without shear deformation; and the shear stiffness is calibrated on a difference the source prints to one significant digit.
